Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniFi Bancorp Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. In order to ensure everyone's questions are addressed, we ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Thank you. I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniFi Bancorp's results for the second quarter of 2024. With me this morning are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; and David Kim, Chief Credit Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. UniFi Bancorp delivered strong performance in the second quarter, driven by our commitment to customer service and operational excellence.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on growing our core businesses, investing in technology and innovation, managing risk effectively, optimizing our capital allocation, and enhancing our employee engagement.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our progress. Overall, we're thrilled with the quarter's results, which underscore resilient execution in a dynamic macroeconomic environment. We achieved record quarterly revenue of $18.7 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 4% sequentially, beating expectations with double-digit growth for the seventh straight quarter. Net interest income rose 15% to $12.4 billion, while non-interest income climbed 8% to $6.3 billion. Diluted EPS hit $1.92, up 14%, and adjusted EPS was $1.98, excluding integration costs from our Midwest Regional Bank acquisition. ROTCE expanded to 15.2%, efficiency ratio improved to 52.4%, and credit quality stayed strong with net charge-offs at 22 basis points and NPL ratio at 0.65%. Segments shone: Consumer and Business Banking grew loans 9% to $285 billion, deposits 6% to $420 billion; Commercial Banking up 11% to $350 billion; Wealth and Investment Management revenues up 10% with AUM at $1.2 trillion. Our tech migration to AWS cut latency 60%, and CET1 stands at 12.8%. We've raised full-year guidance to adjusted EPS $7.85-$8.00 and revenue growth 11-13%.

These results reflect disciplined growth across our diversified franchise. I'll now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results and key aspects like credit quality, loan outlook, technology impacts, and reserves in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. UniFi Bancorp reported net income of $1.92 billion for the second quarter, or $1.92 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 15% due to loan growth and improved net interest margin of 3.45%, up 12 basis points sequentially. Non-interest income was up 8%, driven by fees. Key performance indicators include ROTCE at 15.2% and efficiency at 52.4%. We are confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Turning now to our credit quality metrics—specifically non-performing loan ratios, net charge-offs, and delinquency rates—I'm pleased to report continued stabilization and modest improvement across our portfolios this quarter. We've navigated persistent inflation, the Fed's 525 basis point hikes since early 2022, and uneven post-pandemic recoveries through proactive risk management, with all metrics trending favorably year-over-year and sequentially.

Our overall NPL ratio stood at 1.24% at quarter-end, down 21 basis points from 1.45% last quarter and 35 basis points from 1.59% a year ago—our lowest since pre-COVID Q4 2019. Excluding government-backed FHA and VA mortgages, core NPL was 0.98%, thanks to disciplined underwriting in consumer and C&I. Net charge-offs were 0.42% of average loans, down from 0.51% prior quarter and flat to 0.43% last year, below our 0.55% through-cycle average and peers like Wells Fargo at 0.58% or regionals at 0.65% per S&P Global. Delinquencies 30-89 days improved to 2.18% from 2.45%, with early-stage at 1.12%.

In consumer lending, 35% of loans including cards, autos, and personal lines, NPLs fell to 1.85% from 2.12%, aided by 3.4% unemployment in Midwest and Southeast footprints and AI-driven collections via Kabbage partnership boosting recoveries 15%. Auto delinquencies rose slightly to 2.85% from high APRs, but we're targeting FICO over 720. CRE at 28% saw NPLs up to 1.05% from 0.92% in office and multifamily coastal markets with high vacancies per CBRE, offset by Midwest industrial strength; we've slowed growth to 2% QoQ and stress-tested offices. C&I pristine at 0.65% NPLs, residential mortgages at 0.72% with fixed rates below 4%. Regionally, Midwest exemplary at 0.95%, Southeast slight uptick mitigated by HELOC mods. Nationally outperforming KBW index at 1.48%.

Our GenAI early warning on FIS Profile flags 25% more risks earlier; ACL at 1.42% or 114% of NPLs with $125 million CECL buffer. Provision $145 million below guide. Forward, NPLs 1.1-1.3%, charge-offs 0.40%, with tech overlays like nCino.

Next, our outlook for loan growth and credit quality remains central as we manage a resilient economy. Our $285 billion loan book positions us for disciplined expansion. Full-year total loan growth 5-7%, tilted higher on easier comps from 4.2% YoY this quarter.

By segment: C&I 35% of portfolio, 7-9% growth on healthcare, tech capex; closed $2.5 billion commitments, DSCR >1.8x, leveraging Treasury APIs with Plaid/Stripe. CRE 28%, 3-5% selectively in multifamily/industrial, pausing office amid 12% delinquencies per MBA, focusing Sun Belt at <65% LTV. Residential/home equity 20%, 4-6% on purchase ramp, digital platform via Blend cuts approvals to 10 days. Consumer 17%, 6-8% on auto inventory normalization and co-branded cards at 28% utilization.

Regionally: U.S. 6-8%, Europe 3-5%, Asia-Pac 8-10%. Cloud-native origination with ML dynamic pricing adds 5-10 bps NIM; Growth Engine targets $15 billion SMB via Experian data.

Credit outlook constructive: charge-offs entered cycle at 22 bps, delinquencies 1.12% down 15 bps YoY, NPL 0.85% below FDIC 1.2%, coverage 2.8x. 2024 charge-offs 20-30 bps, PCL $1.2-1.4 billion with releases as unemployment peaks 4.2%. Consumer pristine, subprime autos 4.1% vs. 5.2%; C&I watch 2.1% contained; CRE office 1.8% stress-tested. ESG underwriting, Graph Neural Nets cut losses 8%, $500 million ops modernization.

This supports ROCE >12%.

As a key pillar, our technology investments are transforming efficiency amid fintech competition. FY spend was $1.2 billion or 8.5% of opex, up from 7.2%: 40% infrastructure/cloud, 30% AI/ML, 20% cyber/RegTech, 10% digital. Ahead of McKinsey median 7%, delivering 3.2x ROI.

CIR improved 210 bps to 56.2%, opex up 2.1% vs. 4.5% revenue growth, FTE down 12% via RPA handling 65 million transactions, cutting loan/KYC costs 28%; revenue/FTE $285k up 11%.

Flagships: 85% cloud migration AWS/Azure/Snowflake cuts infra 22%, Temenos supports ISO 20022, STP failures to 0.8%. GenAI chatbot 45% Tier 1 inquiries, NPS +8 to 72; ML fraud saves $240 million, false positives 0.4%. Embedded finance with Plaid/Stripe $450 million fees, PSD2 growth 25%.

Regional: NA RegTech cuts compliance 18%; Europe API 2.5 million users; Asia mobile 40% digital surge; EM blockchain 22% savings. 2024 $1.4 billion spend targets CIR 54.7%, mid-teens ROE.

Now, on reserves: Q2 provision $285 million build vs. $150 million release last year, YTD $780 million up 15%, reflecting CECL models amid low charge-offs 28 bps below 45 bps average.

Build drivers: $120 million CRE office delinquencies up to 0.85%, higher PD/LGD on 2021-22 vintages; $95 million consumer cards to 2.1%, autos limited; $30 million C&I release. Macro stress: 50 bps hike, 3.5% inflation, 4.2% unemployment; U.S. 70% of build.

ACL $12.4 billion, 1.22% loans up 7 bps, above 1.10% peer median. Coverage: 285% NPLs (NPLs $4.35 billion or 43 bps), 162% criticized; consumer 2.45%, CRE 1.05%, C&I 0.85%. Compared to peers: ACL/loans 1.22% vs. 1.12%, ACL/NPLs 285% vs. 250%, NCOs 28 bps vs. 35 bps, delinq 1.45% vs. 1.55%.

ML enhancements with Black Knight/Moody's cut uncertainty 18%; exiting $2.5 billion CRE, CET1 11.8%. Proactive positioning for 2024.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. As Chief Risk Officer, I would like to briefly discuss our risk management framework. We continue to prioritize proactive risk identification and mitigation. Our key focus areas include cybersecurity enhancements and CRE exposure monitoring. We remain vigilant in monitoring emerging risks like inflation persistence and geopolitical tensions, adapting strategies with advanced analytics and stress testing.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, that is one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from John Martinez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Martinez:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on loan growth expectations across segments?

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. We're guiding 5-7% full-year total loan growth, with C&I leading at 7-9% on strong middle-market demand in healthcare and tech capex—we closed $2.5 billion new commitments with solid DSCRs. CRE more modest 3-5%, selective in multifamily and industrial while pausing office. Residential 4-6% on purchases, consumer 6-8% via autos and cards. This is risk-adjusted, profitable growth leveraging our digital tools for better origination.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your expectations for technology spend and efficiency improvements going forward?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Emily. We're committing $1.4 billion in 2024, up from $1.2 billion, focused on quantum-resistant cyber, ESG platforms, and further cloud/AI scaling. Expect another 150 bps CIR compression to 54.7%, building on this quarter's gains from RPA, GenAI chatbots handling 45% inquiries, and embedded finance adding fees. This positions us for ROE expansion even with rate plateaus.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Hayes with KBW. Please go ahead.

Robert Hayes:
Can you comment on the credit quality of your CRE portfolio?

David Kim:
Good morning, Robert. Our CRE book at 28% of loans shows resilience overall, with NPLs at 1.05% this quarter, up modestly from office/multifamily in coastal high-vacancy areas, but offset by strong Midwest industrial. Delinquencies managed through slowed originations at 2% QoQ versus peers' 4%, LTV caps at 65%, and rigorous stress testing for 20% value declines and 10% vacancy spikes. Coverage robust, and we're shifting to floating rates for hedges—quality remains ahead of peers.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your interest in UniFi Bancorp. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
